Class EvaluatedExpressionClassNames

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.inject.annotation.EvaluatedExpressionClassNames
@Internal public final class EvaluatedExpressionClassNames extends Object
Names the classes generated for evaluated expressions after what declares them: the class declaring the annotated element, the element, the annotation and its member, for example test.$Foo$Expr$field$name$Value$value$0123456789abcdef. The name does not depend on the other sources of the compilation or on the order elements are visited in, so the compilation of a class and the compilation of a subclass that reads it from a class file give an expression the same name, and a class compiled again keeps the names of its expression classes.

The element is described by the language, as segments separated by $, with the erased signature of a method or constructor in parentheses: type, field$name, method$name(java.lang.String,int), constructor(int)$param0. The signature only goes into the hash at the end of the name, which also covers the annotation's package and the expression, so overloads, annotations of the same simple name and repeated annotations give distinct names, and a class of a name holds the expression the name was given for.

5.3.0
